argument_text: Here own-nature alone is supremely adoptable: light-nature of all things, since non-light cannot be nature. And it is not many, since no other natures enter light and natures do not differ; place and time too do not divide it, since they too are light-natured. Hence one light alone — and it is consciousness, since consciousness is of the nature of thing-manifestation; here for all there is no dispute. And that light is not dependent, since being-illumined is dependence, since illuminedness needs another light, and since no other light at all exists. Hence autonomous is the one light, and through autonomy alone, free from limitation by place, time, and form, all-pervading, eternal, of all-form-formless-nature. Of it autonomy is bliss-power; its wonder is will-power; light-nature is consciousness-power; grasp is knowledge-power; all-form-fitness is action-power. Thus though endowed with chief powers, really will-knowledge-action-powered, unlimited, the light resting in its own bliss is Śiva-natured. He alone, through autonomy manifesting self contracted, is called atom. And again he manifests own self autonomously — whereby he shines as unlimited-light-Śiva-nature itself. There too, through autonomy, he manifests own self without means or with means; and with means — will, knowing, or action as approach: hence threefoldness of immersion by śāmbhava-śākta-āṇava distinction. Therein all four forms too, in order, here are taught. The self, light-bodied, this Śiva, autonomous — by autonomy-play's force having hidden own nature, which again would spread forth full, that by sequence-nosequence force or threefold.
